figures.finding: An individual pays 10 cents a dollar on taxable income up to NZD 10,000, 20 cents from 10,000 to 20,000 and 30 cents above, as an effective rate on the whole income; a low-income rebate (up to NZD 2,000 outside the public service, up to 1,000 otherwise) reduces it for incomes up to 20,000.
figures.applies: Income Tax Act 1961 Schedules 1 and 3 as consolidated in the Niue Legislation Act 2019; no later amendment was found on the Ministry of Finance's site.

sources.said: On so much income as – The rate of tax for every dollar is – is not more than $10,000 10 cents is more than $10,000 but is not more than $20,000 20 cents is more than $20,000 30 cents

On all income not included within clause 2 the rate of income tax for every dollar of taxable income shall be the effective rate of tax ascertained by calculating tax on that income in accordance with the rates of tax specified in Part B
primary employment earnings are not derived from employment in the Niue Public Service or a statutory body $20,000 a year or less $2,000

figures.finding: The tax year runs from 1 April to 31 March; the individual return (TF1) is due 31 May and any balance by 31 January.

sources.said: “year” means a year commencing on 1 April and ending on 31 March, both of these days being included;
Tax Filing Due Dates 31 May Income Tax Form TF1
Payment Due Dates 31January Income Tax debt payments

figures.finding: Employers deduct tax from salary and wages (PAYE, Part 6A of the act) and pay it by the 20th of the following month; a secondary employment taxed under code SEC is withheld at 10 cents a dollar.

sources.said: In the case of an employee to whom the tax code “SEC” under section 113D applies, the rate of withholding from the salary or wages or other source deduction payment of the employee arising from an employment other than the employee’s primary employment is 10 cants in every dollar.

figures.finding: Niue Consumption Tax is 12.5%; registration is required once taxable supplies reach NZD 200,000 in 12 months.

sources.said: a person exceeds the registration threshold in a particular period if the total value of taxable supplies made or reasonably expected to be made by the person during the period is equal to or greater than $200,000.

figures.finding: The Financial Secretary may withhold up to 10% of any account paid to a supplier of goods or services to the Niue Government, as a payment towards that supplier's income tax for the year, particularly where the supplier is non-compliant or in arrears.
figures.applies: Suppliers (including freelancers) paid by the Niue Government (Income Tax Act 1961, s. 113R)

sources.said: 113R Withholding payments (1) The Financial Secretary may exercise discretion and withhold up to 10 percent of the total account to be paid to a supplier of goods or services to the Niue Government, as a contribution towards the total tax payable by the supplier in respect of his income in that income year.
